blocks.x: Agentic AI & Hyperautomation applied to Capabilities. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

In Manufacturing & Industrial, agentic ai & hyperautomation turns knowledge work into orchestrated autonomy. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: agentic process automation, digital workforce & multi-agent orchestration, decision intelligence systems — delivered on Dataq Swarm and Dataq Nexus and Dataq Compass with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Planning by spreadsheet under volatility

Planners fight demand volatility, material shortages and changeovers in spreadsheets; scheduling knowledge lives in two veterans' heads. OEE losses from changeover and waiting are structurally accepted.
Maintenance planning reactive
PM schedules fire by calendar while failures happen by physics; planners cannot see which assets are trending toward failure this week.
Brownfield instrumentation gap
Critical assets run uninstrumented because gut-and-replace is unthinkable; the data that twins and models need does not exist, and downtime for retrofit is unaffordable.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

The delivery pattern composes 7 services from the Agentic AI & Hyperautomation tower — Agentic Process Automation, Digital Workforce & Multi-Agent Orchestration, Decision Intelligence Systems, Intelligent Document Processing as the usual core — sequenced through the Dataq Method with sector controls: NIS2 (EU operators) obligations shape the design from the first sprint.

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: NIS2 (EU operators) and IEC 62443. Industrial cybersecurity zones-and-conduits for OT estates. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Delivery follows the same weekly rhythm on every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
